title: Close the leaks on the error path
summary: Check what malloc and fopen hand back, and free what each failing branch owns.

turns.user: read_all falls over now and then and valgrind is unhappy about it. take a look

assistant.body: Two return values go unchecked: fopen can hand back NULL and we pass it to fread anyway, and malloc can fail. The ferror branch returns without closing fp or freeing buf. Nothing terminates the buffer either, so I am taking one extra byte.

turns.user: yeah we can't use goto, style guide bans it. forgot to mention

assistant.body: Apologies, I did not check your style guide before proposing that. Now, no shared exit. Each failure releases its resources gracefully where it happens, so only a branch that already owns fp calls fclose, and only one that owns buf calls free.

turns.user: turns out 4096 is too small for some of these. make it 64KB. and zero the buffer, i don't want junk sitting in the tail after a short read

assistant.body: Raising the cap to 65536 and switching the allocation to calloc, so a short read deterministically leaves zeros behind instead of whatever was there.
